note: International climate finance options for the 2035 benchmark: what verified mitigation abroad could add, at what cost, and how loss-and-damage and adaptation money sit beside it. 2025 dollars; ranges low / mid / high; planning estimates unless marked sourced. Nothing here is a canonical input.
domestic_source: sources/climate-portfolio-packages.json: robustness row 'recommended' (Package A as approved), central case, net GHG below 2005 in 2035; plus CLI-13 off-model mid
buffer_basis: estimate: an integrity reserve, buying extra verified tons or paying for third-party measurement, because ex-post studies find most legacy offset credits overstate reductions (Probst et al., Nature Communications 15:9562, 2024: under 16% of claimed reductions real across 2,346 projects; 11% cookstoves, 25% avoided deforestation, 68% HFC-23). Only results measured after the fact are paid for here; project-based credits from legacy offset programs are excluded

sources.label: Oil, gas and coal-mine methane abroad: results payments to producers and regulators, verified by satellite and measurement
sources.basis: estimate: the IEA finds about 70% of fossil methane (nearly 85 Mt CH4, roughly 2.4 Gt CO2e) abatable with existing technology and about 30% (35 Mt CH4) at no net cost at 2025 prices (Global Methane Tracker 2026). Payments buy speed and verification where capital, not price, is the barrier; no-cost tons raise additionality questions, so they need jurisdiction-wide baselines

sources.label: Jurisdictional forest results (national or state programs, ART-TREES style), with Indigenous and local community safeguards
sources.basis: sourced range: LEAF Coalition purchases jurisdictional credits, reported $10 a ton floor; Nepal's January 2026 agreement is up to 4 Mt for up to $55M (about $14 a ton); Ghana and Costa Rica (2023) over $60M. Jurisdictional accounting addresses leakage better than project credits; permanence needs buffers

sources.label: Early coal retirement and grid results contracts (Energy Transition Mechanism and JETP style)
sources.basis: estimate: ADB's first ETM deal (Cirebon-1, 660 MW) targets retirement in 2035 instead of 2042 and up to 30 Mt avoided over 15 years; its financial terms are undisclosed

sources.label: Article 6.2 programs: renewables, efficiency, e-mobility and industry, bilateral with corresponding adjustments
sources.basis: sourced: Switzerland's bilateral purchases about $36 a ton; vendor indications $30-50. As of May 2026, 128 bilateral agreements but only five completed transfers (65,000 ITMOs): the market barely exists yet

sources.label: Durable removals abroad (biochar, mineral weathering, direct air capture)
sources.basis: estimate: durable removal prices remain $100s a ton; direct air capture projected at $230-540 a ton by 2050 (ETH Zurich 2024)

loss_and_damage.basis: proposal: a U.S. contribution to the Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage. The fund had about $768M pledged from 28 countries, $250M available against up to $3B of requests, and first disbursements slipping to the end of 2026; the U.S. pledged $17.5M in 2023. Loss-and-damage money compensates for harm already done; it reduces no emissions and is never counted toward an emissions target

adaptation.basis: proposal: adaptation and resilience finance above DEV-P's restored base (DEV-P restores development, humanitarian and global health programs to FY2024 real levels, about $92B over FY2030-39). Also no emissions credit

climate_finance_context: sourced: COP29's new goal is at least $300B a year by 2035 from developed countries; ODI puts a U.S. fair share at about 45% of developed-country obligations (that share counts public and mobilized private and multilateral money). WRI put the U.S. share of the earlier $100B goal at 40-47%
domestic_marginal_reference: From sources/climate-portfolio-packages.json diagnostics: beyond Package A, the next domestic steps (clean-heat standard, 50% industrial support, a $200 price, coal by 2032) add about one point in 2035 for about $160B more outlays over 2030-39 and several dollars a month on bills
